name: Route 66
title: Route 66 — One Stop at a Time
description: Route 66 roadside memories from Missouri to the Santa Monica Pier, arranged east to west from separate trips: Devil’s Elbow, Cadillac Ranch, the Blue Hole, Winslow, and more filmed stops.
hero_alt: A scene from the film Route 66, One Stop at a Time.
intro: Route 66 gave them more reasons to stop than to hurry. These films gather roadside memories from Missouri to the Santa Monica Pier: small towns, old bridges, Oklahoma neon, Cadillac Ranch, the Blue Hole, Lowell Observatory — where Pluto was discovered in 1930 — and the people and places they wanted to remember.

The footage comes from separate trips, arranged east to west. It is not one continuous drive, and they have not driven every mile. The map line follows Route 66 roughly between the stops that appear in the films. It is a guide to the road, not a record of a single journey.

stops.name: World’s Largest Rocking Chair
stops.note: The film caption reads “The Red Rocker Cuba, MO.” The chair stands at the Route 66 Fanning Outpost: 42 feet tall and steel-framed, built in 2008 as a Guinness Record breaker.

stops.name: Mule Trading Post
stops.note: A Route 66 stop in Rolla, seen in the Missouri film.

stops.name: Totem Pole Trading Post
stops.note: A Route 66 trading post on Martin Springs Drive in Rolla, seen in the Missouri film.

then_and_now.text: The trading post closed in September 2024, and the building was demolished in May 2025.
then_and_now.source_note: Ron Warnick, “Totem Pole Trading Post in Rolla, one of Twin Bridges near Catoosa torn down,” Route 66 News, May 14, 2025: Josh Thompson photographed the demolition on May 7, 2025; the post closed in late September 2024. Closure on Sept. 30, 2024 also reported by Allison Skinner, Phelps County Focus, Sept. 23, 2024, https://phelpscountyfocus.com/2024/09/23/open-since-1933-totem-pole-trading-post-doors-closing-sept-30/.

stops.name: Devil’s Elbow
stops.note: A sharp bend in the Big Piney River that gave this community its name, and the historic Devil’s Elbow Bridge.

stops.name: Uranus Fudge Factory & General Store
stops.note: A humorous roadside stop with gift shops, photo ops, and novelty fun.

stops.name: Marshfield
stops.note: A scale replica of the Hubble Space Telescope, honoring local legend Edwin Hubble.

stops.name: Galena
stops.note: Named in the Kansas chapter of the east-to-west film, together with Rainbow Bridge.

stops.name: Cars on the Route
stops.note: A restored Kan-O-Tex station in Galena, seen in the Missouri film. The Galena stop above is from the east-to-west film.

stops.name: Rainbow Bridge
stops.note: Named in the Kansas chapter of the east-to-west film, together with Galena.

stops.name: Phillips 66 Visitors’ Center
stops.note: Just over the border from Missouri. A restored 1930s Phillips 66 gas station, now a Route 66 Visitors’ Center, run by volunteers.

stops.name: Ed Galloway’s Totem Pole Park
stops.note: A folk-art park east of Foyil, seen in the Oklahoma film.

stops.name: The Blue Whale
stops.note: An iconic Route 66 stop.

stops.name: Route 66 Rising
stops.note: A sculpture at the Cyrus Avery Traffic Circle in Tulsa.

stops.name: The Golden Driller
stops.note: A tall oil-worker statue at the Tulsa Expo Center. The Oklahoma film starts here.

stops.name: Buck Atom’s Cosmic Curios
stops.note: On Route 66 in Tulsa.

stops.name: Pops 66
stops.note: A Route 66 restaurant and gas station in Arcadia, marked by a tall soda bottle.

stops.name: Braum’s Giant Milk Bottle
stops.note: The Milk Bottle Grocery on Classen Boulevard, with a Braum’s milk bottle on the roof.

stops.name: Lucille’s Service Station
stops.note: A historic Route 66 service station near Hydro, also known as the Provine Service Station.

stops.name: Cadillac Ranch
